'''Azusawake-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (あずさわけのみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}, {{ill|To-shima, Tokyo|Q1143112|qid=Q1143112}}. It is the village’s {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} (tutelary deity) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=guardian shrine}}<ref name="toshima">[https://www.toshimamura.org/tourism/watch/shrine.html Visiting Shrines] - Toshima Village</ref><ref name="tokyo">[https://www.kankyo1.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/naturepark/know/park/introduction/kokuritsu/fujihakone/toshima/tourism.html Tourism in Toshima] - Tokyo Metropolitan Government Tourism Bureau</ref>.

It is identified with a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of the same name<ref name="jinjacho">[http://www.tokyo-jinjacho.or.jp/tosho/2843/ Azusawake-no-Mikoto Shrine] - Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines</ref><ref name="jinjacho2">[http://tosho.tokyo-jinjacho.or.jp/toshima.html Azusawake-no-Mikoto Shrine] - Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines (Island Feature Edition)</ref>.

=== Overview ===
The date of foundation is unknown, but as it is identified with a Shikinaisha, its origins are thought to date back to before ancient times. It has long been affectionately known to villagers as “Myōjin-sama.”

It is known for the New Year’s Day (January 1) “Jikkuwa-bi” fire ritual, as well as the “Yamamawari” (mountain circuit) custom during the first three days of the New Year (January 1–3), in which people visit the following shrines located in the southern and western parts of the island:
* First Deity: Azusawake-no-Mikoto Hongū
* Second Deity: Ōyama-Koyama Shrine
* Third Deity: Orinobori Shrine
<ref name="toshima"/><ref name="tokyo"/>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* **Azusawake-no-Mikoto** (あづさわけのみこと) – A pioneering deity of the Izu Islands and a prince of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611}}.
* **Orinobori-no-Mikoto** (おりのぼりのみこと) – His consort.
